title: JavaScript Fundamentals Quiz
description: Test your understanding of JavaScript fundamentals.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a variable that can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: The let keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned.

questions.question: What is the result of typeof null in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Due to a historical JavaScript bug, typeof null returns object.

questions.question: Which method adds an element to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push() adds one or more elements to the end of an array.

questions.question: What does === check in JavaScript?
options: Whether two variables have the same name
questions.explanation: Strict equality checks whether two values are equal without performing type coercion.

questions.question: Which method selects the first element matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector() returns the first element matching the specified CSS selector.

questions.question: What does the map() method return?
questions.explanation: map() creates and returns a new array containing the results of calling a callback on each array element.

questions.question: Which event occurs when a user changes the value of a textarea?
questions.explanation: The input event fires when the value of an input or textarea changes through user interaction.

questions.question: What does preventDefault() do?
questions.explanation: preventDefault() prevents the default browser behaviour associated with a cancelable event.

questions.question: Which data structure follows the Last In, First Out (LIFO) principle?
questions.explanation: A stack follows LIFO: the last element inserted is the first one removed.

questions.question: What does the filter() method return?
options: A new array containing elements that pass a condition
The original array with deleted elements
questions.explanation: filter() creates a new array containing elements for which the callback returns true.
